tarifs.lead: Prices are a guide: every pair and every bag is different. We look at the item with you and give you the price before touching anything.

atelier.title: A neighbourhood workshop that opens before work
atelier.text: At 34 rue Gaulthier de Rumilly, the workshop opens at 7:15am and stays open through lunch. Drop your shoes off on the way to work, pick them up on the way home. Small repairs are often done while you wait.

cles.title: A spare key in the time it takes to have a coffee
cles.text: Flat keys for your home, cellar or letterbox, high-security keys with the owner’s card, car keys and building fobs depending on the model. Bring the original key and we’ll check with you that it can be copied.

cuir.title: Leather can be cared for, not thrown away
cuir.text: A faded bag, a seam coming apart, a belt that’s too long, a broken zip: leather takes repair very well. Dyeing, stitching, new handles: we’ll tell you honestly what’s worth doing.

metier.title: Master craftsman is more than a title
metier.text: The Maître Artisan title is awarded by the French Chamber of Trades and Crafts. It recognises qualifications and years of practice in the trade. In the workshop it simply means this: we take the time to look, we tell you what can be fixed and what isn’t worth the money, and we do the work by hand.
points: Repair rather than replace: a good pair, resoled, goes on for years.
The price is given before we start, no surprise when you collect.
Care advice so the repair lasts.

tips.title: Four habits that make your shoes last

items.title: Rotate your pairs
items.text: Leather needs a day to dry out. Two pairs worn in turn last more than twice as long.

items.title: Wooden shoe trees
items.text: Slipped in as soon as you take your shoes off, they keep the shape and absorb moisture.

items.title: Protectors on new leather
items.text: On a leather sole, a protector fitted early guards the front of the foot and delays resoling.

items.title: Away from the radiator
items.text: When wet, let them dry in the open air, stuffed with newspaper. Direct heat cracks leather.

infos.title: Come to the workshop
infos.accessText: Henriville neighbourhood, just south of the city centre, a few minutes’ walk from Amiens station. Street parking nearby.
infos.mapTitle: Map to Cordonnerie Henriville, 34 rue Gaulthier de Rumilly, Amiens

items.a: No. The workshop welcomes you without an appointment, Tuesday to Saturday, from 7:15am to 7pm without a break.

items.q: How long does a repair take?
items.a: Keys, watch batteries, heel tips and belts are often done while you wait. Resoling or dyeing takes a few days. We give you the pick-up date when you drop the item off.

items.q: How do I get a quote?
items.a: Come to the workshop with the item, or send 1 to 3 photos through the quote form. We reply with a price and a turnaround time, and nothing starts without your go-ahead.

Common flat keys (home, cellar, letterbox), high-security keys with the owner’s card, some car keys and building fobs depending on the model. Bring the original key and we’ll tell you straight away if it’s possible.

items.q: Which payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Cash and card. You pay when you collect, once the repair is done.

items.q: What if I forget to collect my shoes?
items.a: Keep the ticket you get when you drop them off. Items are kept at the workshop; after several months without news, we get in touch. Drop by or call if in doubt.

ressemelage.metaTitle: Shoe Resoling in Amiens, Heels & Protectors | Cordonnerie Henriville
ressemelage.metaDescription: Leather or rubber resoling in Amiens by a master shoemaker: heels, sole protectors, stitching. Quote by photo, no appointment, Henriville neighbourhood.
ressemelage.title: Shoe resoling in Amiens
ressemelage.intro: A good pair deserves more than one life. When the sole is worn or has a hole, we replace it and keep the upper, and your shoes are good for years more.

list.title: Leather resoling
list.text: For leather-soled dress shoes: we replace the sole like for like.

list.title: Rubber resoling
list.text: More grip, longer wear, ideal for Amiens winters.

list.title: Heels and heel tips
list.text: Men’s heels, women’s heel tips: often done while you wait.

list.title: Sole protectors
list.text: A thin protective sole fitted under the front of the foot, on new or barely worn leather.

how.title: The sole is getting thin
how.text: Press the middle of the forefoot: if it feels soft like cardboard, it’s time.

how.title: The heel wears at an angle
how.text: Don’t let the wear reach the sole: a heel is quick and cheap to change.

how.title: Before the hole
how.text: A sole with a hole lets water in and damages the insole: resole before.

ressemelage.related: Not sure about your pair? Send a photo of the sole and we’ll tell you what’s possible.
